title: 911 Calls Lead Officers into 100 Round Shootout
description:
Submit a tip! Tips@Midwest-Safety.com

Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this. 

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com. 

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

It also shows officers chased a man through Goodale Park shortly after 319 in the morning, held him at gunpoint near Park Street, and arrested him as a primary shooting suspect. However, news reports do not mention this person, or whether he was charged or released. The only person identified as a suspect in news reports is Jalen Bradley, the 20-year-old we saw apprehended. Ten people were shot, all survived, and no officers were injured. The shooting near the Guildhouse and the one near United Dairy Farmers are seemingly considered separate, unrelated events. But the violence did not end there. News reports say two additional deadly shootings occurred, causing three total deaths, with the third shooting happening within an hour of the first. Reports say officers were so overwhelmed with existing calls that no cruisers could be sent at first. In that shooting, five people were shot, and two died. 28-year-old victim, Talon Rowland, was allegedly killed by a suspected shooter, 29-year-old Keith Pleasant, who reportedly died from self-inflicted wounds. The fourth shooting occurred about two hours after the first. 36-year-old David Davis was allegedly shot and killed by a 34-year-old man after an argument, but the charges were later dropped for undisclosed reasons. The man apprehended in this video, Jalen Bradley and his sister, Jadon Bradley, are claiming innocence and suing the department and the involved officers for more than $14 million. According to a lawsuit filed in May of 2024, the same day the Franklin County Prosecutor's Office confirmed the officers would not face criminal The lawsuit states Jalen and his sister were walking when a group of men began shooting at them causing injury. Ohio allows any qualifying adult to open carry a handgun without a permit. By default, Jalen returned fire with his legally owned firearm in self-defense. The suit says officers, unaware of what was happening, fired at Jalen and his sister, hitting Jalen 11 times, leaving him paralyzed. It also claims Jalen never fired at officers, contradicting reports. Dispatch notes show bullets were found in the building behind the officers, but do not identify whether they came from Jalen's gun or from any of the 15 to 20 other people who may have fired that night. The suspect vehicle likely passed through this area, but no official information has been released. So far, the only released angle of the interaction comes from Officer Harmon's body camera. Even when playing back the footage at 25% of the speed, it is difficult to determine the truth. Months after the lawsuit was filed, the three involved officers received an award of Valor at the 2004 Law Enforcement Training Symposium. The Distinguished Law Enforcement Award for Valor honors a police officer who, despite risk of his or her own safety, demonstrates extraordinary courage in protecting other people from harm. This evening we honor three officers of the Columbus Division of Police, Carl Harmon, Ian Mansberger, and Jacob Velas. They identified the act of shooters in open fire. As Harmon reached the west side of North High Street, he saw that the primary suspect was on the ground badly wounded, his gun thrown to the side. But as he and Velas scanned for additional threats, the downed suspect raised a pistol and fired several shots at them. Columbus Police Lieutenant Brian Steele, president of FOP Capital City Lodge number nine, said it was one of the most chaotic events he had seen in his 20 years as a police officer. And retired detective John Witherspoon said it was amazing that no bystanders were injured. The civil suit is still ongoing and reports do not indicate if anyone has been charged for the shooting.
